column3: NSGA-II in which dominance is replaced by Deb's rules: feasible beats infeasible, smaller violation beats larger, otherwise Pareto dominance.
column4: • No penalty parameter; P6 HV 1.019 †.; • On P7 returns 85 points (HV 0.699) – far better than non-elitist NSGA's 25 †.; • Infeasible solutions still guide the search through their violation.; • Same cost and complexity as NSGA-II.; • P5 results identical to penalty NSGA-II here (HV 0.828) – the rule never hurts †.
column5: • P6 IGD 0.006 is slightly worse than penalty NSGA-II's 0.006 †.; • If the feasible region is tiny or disconnected, early populations contain no feasible points and diversity is lost.; • Violation measures of different constraints must be aggregated and scaled.; • Equality constraints need a tolerance.; • P7: only 85 of 100 individuals are non-dominated after 10,000 evaluations †.
column7: Problems where infeasible regions must be crossed to reach disconnected parts.

column3: Particles move by v = wv + c₁r₁(pbest−x) + c₂r₂(gbest−x); leaders come from a grid-based archive; turbulence mutation decays.
column4: • Fast: 0.8s for 10,000 evaluations †.; • Good convergence on P5 (HV 0.830, IGD 0.011 vs MOGWO's 0.031) †.; • Few parameters, easy for real variables.; • Dense, even front on P4 (Spacing 0.008) †.; • Archive gives elitism.
column5: • IGD on P4 (0.007) is worse than SPEA2's (0.004) †.; • Velocity can leave the bounds (needs reflection).; • Real variables only (binary/perm need other variants).; • Premature convergence if w and the archive leader pressure are high.; • The archive cap (100) limits the output: 100 points on P5 †.
column6: Continuous, smooth problems with a modest budget (P4, P5).

column3: Three leaders (α, β, δ) from the archive guide every wolf by encircling; the control factor a falls from 2 to 0.
column4: • Few parameters; P5 HV 0.791 in 0.6s †.; • Exploration → exploitation schedule built in.; • Works on binary problems via transfer function (P9).; • Archive-based leaders provide elitism.; • Handles binary P9 via a sigmoid transfer (found 5 subsets) †.
column5: • P5 IGD 0.031 is worse than NSGA-II's 0.013 and MOPSO's 0.011 †.; • Binary P9 run found only 5 non-dominated subsets and cost 12.4s for 3,000 evaluations (5-NN CV) †.; • Mean of leaders drags solutions to the centre of the archive → weak spread at the ends.; • Sigmoid binary version loses the geometric meaning of the update.; • Time-based schedule needs the budget in advance.
column6: Continuous constrained design problems with limited tuning effort.

column3: Employed bees perturb one dimension toward a neighbour, onlookers favour better ranks, scouts restart stagnant sources; dominance-based greedy selection.
column4: • Strong results: P3 HV 0.534, IGD 0.007 † and P6 IGD 0.004 †.; • Very fast (0.4s) †.; • Only the limit and colony size to tune.; • Scouts prevent stagnation.; • Dense archive.
column5: • One-dimension moves converge slowly on rotated problems.; • Dominance-only greedy rule loses information when solutions are non-dominated (random 50 % acceptance).; • Overshoots the budget slightly (10,050 evaluations) because a cycle evaluates 2–3 N points †.; • Real variables only.; • P3 IGD 0.007 trails MO-TLBO (0.005) †.

column3: Two pheromone matrices (distance, time) and heuristics; each ant uses its own weight λ; archive-based pheromone deposit.
column4: • Finds the 10-point front of P8 (HV 0.757) †.; • Cheapest of the routing algorithms here (1.9s) †.; • Heuristic information speeds up tour construction.; • Different λ per ant spreads the search along the front.; • Natural for permutation problems.
column5: • Permutation/graph problems only.; • Several parameters (α, β, ρ, ant count, bounds).; • Pheromone matrices cost O(n²) each and the deposit rule is heuristic.; • No advantage on 15 cities: NSGA-II with order crossover gets the same HV (0.757) †.; • Python tour construction makes it slower than NSGA-II (1.9s vs 0.7s) †.
column6: Routing problems with good heuristic information.
